name: Sayyid Qutb
role: Egyptian Islamist writer and Muslim Brotherhood ideologue (1906-1966)
summary: Qutb, an Egyptian literary critic turned Islamist thinker, held that all authority belongs to God and that modern societies, Western, communist and nominally Muslim alike, are jahili because they let men legislate. He called for an Islamic order under the Shari'a, to be spread by preaching and, where political power blocks it, by force, and rejected nationalism, capitalism and communism. He was executed in 1966.

property-fundamental.rationale: He approves private ownership as legitimate but subjects it to checks, including the state taking the rich's surplus in hardship, so the record points both ways.

traditional-family.rationale: He says the Islamic system takes great care to strengthen the family, the tie on which human life is built, and protects it from every weakening influence.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He treats same-sex practice as perversion that Islam punishes, which is incompatible with legalising same-sex marriage.

more-religion-public.rationale: He demands that every aspect of life, law included, be placed under God's sovereignty and the Shari'a.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He says the soil of the homeland has no value in itself and that a Muslim's only tie is belief, not national tradition.

revolution-justified.rationale: He describes the Islamic message as revolutionary and says it must abolish by force the political systems that bar people from it.

democracy-best.rationale: He holds that any system whose final decisions and sources of authority are human usurps God's sovereignty, and says Western democracy has become infertile.

political-violence-never.rationale: He says the Islamic movement uses physical power and jihad to abolish the authorities of the jahili order, rejecting a purely non-violent road.

separate-church-state.rationale: He holds that no law may come from any source but God and treats societies that confine God's rule to the heavens as jahili.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He says a society is Muslim only if it accepts the Shari'a without question and rejects all other laws in any shape or form.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He says a Muslim has no nationality except belief and that Islam eliminated relationships based on blood, race and country.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He rejects the materialist interpretation of history and "scientific socialism" as a jahili view, holding values fixed above economic conditions.

civilizational-union.rationale: He teaches that all believers form one community in Dar-ul-Islam bound by belief across races and countries, with the movement to extend over the whole earth.

collective-farming.rationale: He cites the failure of Soviet collective farming as a system against human nature.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He holds the Muslim homeland is a base from which the movement is carried throughout the earth, though he frames this as spreading Islam rather than national gain.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The reference work reports he opposed Israel's creation and tied it to US and Soviet imperialism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He says the call is to accept the Shari'a without any question and that it does not rest on persuasion by its reasonableness.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He says a woman's normal place is the home, with the man bound to support her financially so she can raise children, and objects to mothers working outside it.

ban-interest.rationale: He argues the Qur'an prohibits all usury at any rate of interest and says faith and a usury-based system cannot exist side by side.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He says Islam came to abolish political systems based on racial and class distinctions and describes Muslim society as an open community of all races.

national-mission.rationale: He describes the land under God's law as the headquarters of a movement to carry its system to all humanity.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He praises the intermingling of races within the Muslim community as its strength, with no trace of racial separation.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He describes zakat and the sharing of state gains with the needy as basic duties, and says the state may take the rich's surplus for the poor in hardship.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He calls the whole modern world, Western and Eastern, jahili and presents Islam's civilization as the only true one.

death-penalty.rationale: He treats stoning of adulterers as the Prophet's final and permanent verdict and defends the mandatory penalties of Islamic law.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He says Islam approves private ownership but subjects it to the rule that wealth must not circulate only among the rich, and gives it a beneficial social role.

women-must-cover.rationale: He says women are ordered to cover head, neck and chest in public as an instruction of the community's law, though he does not call for covering the whole body.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: He teaches that ties of blood, language and soil are to be eliminated as the basis of human relationships in favour of the bond of belief.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He rejects the materialistic interpretation of history, saying moral standards do not depend on environment or economic stage.

ban-cartels.rationale: He says Islam strictly forbids monopoly and usury as the tools that keep wealth among the rich, which is close to but not the same as breaking up cartels to protect competition.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He says authorities are to be obeyed only while they accept God's sovereignty and implement His guidance, and not in what is forbidden.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He says Islam's system is not a Western invention and that the Islamic order is unique, with Western institutions exhausted.

filial-duty.rationale: He says the divine relationship does not prohibit a Muslim from treating his parents with kindness, though belief ranks first.

non-intervention.rationale: He holds jihad must abolish usurping systems of human rule everywhere in the world, whatever the state.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He says the servants of Zionism and Christian fanaticism and the "people of earlier revelations" work together in secret for the total destruction of the Islamic faith.

religious-nation.rationale: He holds that belief alone forms the community, one party of God, in which a Muslim has no nationality except his belief.

religion-illusion.rationale: He treats the view that religion is a trap set by capitalists or an illusion as Marxist malice and rejects it, holding faith to be the basis of human society.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He calls both communist and capitalist societies products of rebellion against God and presents the Islamic system as unique, neither capitalist nor communist.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: He treats the Qur'anic verse on the "two who are guilty" as referring to homosexual men, accepts punishment of it, and calls such practice perverse.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He says the Islamic movement must use physical force to abolish the organizations and authorities of the jahili system that do not rule by God's law.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He says Western civilization has lost its life-giving values and that the Islamic way of life alone can replace it, with Muslim society distinct from its jahiliyyah.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He writes that sovereignty belongs to God alone in all human affairs and that God's revealed law is the source of all authority.

racial-franchise.rationale: He describes the Muslim community as one in which peoples of every race and colour were equal members, with no basis in race.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He says the detailed rulings and laws remain the same for all time while only the basic principles frame life.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: He says the man is placed in charge of the family and may use graded disciplinary measures, while the wife keeps her own civil status.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: He says there is only one party of God and all others are parties of Satan and rebellion, making the struggle over authority a struggle of faith.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He says the new leadership must combine material progress with high ideals and faith as a way of life, as human beings are more than animals.

racial-pride.rationale: He says the first Muslims became free of pride of lineage and nationality and that Islam removes such low traits.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He says Islamic jihad is not merely defensive war and mocks those who confine it so, as defeated apologists.

language-defines-nation.rationale: He argues the Prophet deliberately avoided Arab nationalism and holds that a Muslim's only nationality is belief, whatever language or country.

premarital-sex.rationale: He comments on the flogging of fornicators and adulterers and describes the prohibition of adultery as part of Islam's aim to eradicate immorality from the community.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: He treats the Qur'an as God's revealed law and constitution to be accepted without question, though he does not set out a rule of literal reading.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: He says the new leadership must keep the material fruits of European genius and add the values of Islam.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: He says jihad must remove by force the political systems that block Islam so that the Shari'a governs civil life everywhere, and rejects limiting it to defence.

religion-from-peoples-character.rationale: He says Islam is not a product of any people's genius, eastern or western, but a universal message from God.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: He says God's bounty is not reserved for any community or group and that membership rests on belief, not people.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: He presents jihad as a duty to abolish tyranny and treats the martyr's death in that cause as honourable.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: He defends the qualified permission of polygamy up to four wives under conditions of fair treatment.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: He rejects any human-sovereign system as usurping God's authority, so promoting liberal democracy abroad contradicts his position.

notes: Searched Milestones in full and the Shade of the Qur'an volumes for Surahs 3, 4, 5, 7, 24, 33 and 57-59 by theme (economy, government, women and family, race and nation, war, law and punishment, minorities). Social Justice in Islam is only on a lending library and could not be read. Surah 2, 9 and 42 commentary texts could not be fetched, so apostasy, shura as a voting rule and jizya details are null. Nothing found on ecology, technology policy, immigration, trade or most modern policy statements, which are null.
